args.body:
Hi Eve! I just visited your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- The blog has a warm, personal feel — it reads like it's written by a real person rather than a content machine.
- Mentioning that hiking is your favorite hobby gives visitors an immediate sense of who you are and what you care about. That's a nice personal touch.

Where I'd suggest some improvement:
- The site is very sparse right now. A short intro about what the blog covers (travel, trail reviews, gear notes, etc.) would help new visitors orient themselves quickly.
- Adding a few recent post titles or links would make the blog feel more active and give readers an easy entry point.
- A couple of photos from your hikes would add a lot of life to the page and make the hobby come through visually.

Overall, a nice foundation for a personal blog — it just needs a bit more content and personality on the surface to really shine. Keep up the hiking stories!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Dora! I've just visited your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- The site is clean and straightforward — it introduces you and your contact details without any clutter, which is a refreshing approach.
- Making your email address easy to find is a practical touch for anyone who wants to get in touch.

Where I'd suggest some improvement:
- The page is very minimal, so it doesn't give visitors much to engage with. A short bio about who you are, what you do, or what you're interested in would make it feel more personal and memorable.
- Adding a few sections or links — for example, projects, a portfolio, photos, or recent updates — would give people a reason to return.
- Some visual design (even simple typography or a header image) would help the site feel more polished and intentional.

Overall, a nice, no-fuss personal site. With a bit more content, it could go from a placeholder into a genuinely interesting home page.

Best,
Emma Johnson
